title: Brown representability criterion for a right adjoint
statement: Let $F:C\to D$ be an exact functor between triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] (categories equipped with shifts and distinguished triangles) with set-indexed coproducts. If $C$ is compactly generated [def-pc-compactly-generated] (generated by a set of compact objects) and $F$ preserves set-indexed coproducts, then $F$ has a right adjoint.

proof.text: For each object d of D, define H_d:C^{op}\to Ab by H_d(c)=Hom_D(F(c),d). Since F is exact and D is triangulated, applying Hom_D(-,d) to the image under F of every distinguished triangle gives the long exact sequence required for H_d to be cohomological.

source.place: Tag 0A8G, Proposition proposition-brown proof; construction of the cohomological Hom functor

proof.text: Because F preserves set-indexed coproducts, for every family (c_i) the canonical map H_d(\bigoplus_i c_i)\to\prod_i H_d(c_i) is the usual Hom-out-of-a-coproduct isomorphism. Thus H_d sends coproducts to products.

source.place: Tag 0A8G, Proposition proposition-brown proof; direct-sum preservation

proof.text: The Brown representability statement [lem-pc-brown-cohomological-representability] applies to H_d by steps 1 and 2. Hence for every d there are an object G(d) of C and natural isomorphisms Hom_D(F(c),d)\cong Hom_C(c,G(d)).

source.place: Tag 0A8G, Proposition proposition-brown, using Lemma lemma-brown (Tag 0A8F)

proof.text: For a morphism u:d\to d' in D, naturality of the representing isomorphisms gives a unique morphism G(u):G(d)\to G(d') whose precomposition action corresponds to postcomposition by u on Hom_D(F(-),-). The identity and composition laws follow by the uniqueness part of representability (Yoneda), so G is a functor and the displayed isomorphisms are natural in both c and d. Therefore F is left adjoint to G, and G is the required right adjoint.
